skills.name: Accounting for financing transactions: capital and loans

note.text:
Financing transactions bring long-term money into the enterprise.
• Capital contributed by the owner: debit 521 Bank (or 571 Cash, or the asset given), credit 101 Capital.
• Loan received from a bank: debit 521 Bank, credit 162 Loans from credit institutions.
• Repayment of the loan: debit 162 Loans, credit 521 Bank. Interest paid is an expense: debit 671 Interest, credit 521 Bank.
Capital and loans are resources (class 1); the money received is in treasury (class 5).

sections.heading: Where the money comes from
sections.text:
A new business needs money to start. The two main long-term sources are the owner's capital and loans.
Both are resources recorded in class {1}: {'101 Capital'} for what the owner puts in, {'162 Loans from credit institutions'} for money borrowed from a bank.

sections.heading: The entries
sections.text:
• Capital paid into the bank: debit {'521 Bank'}, credit {'101 Capital'}. Paid in cash: debit {'571 Cash'}. If the owner brings a car, debit {'245 Transport equipment'}.
• Loan received: debit {'521 Bank'}, credit {'162 Loans'}.
• Loan repaid: debit {'162 Loans'}, credit {'521 Bank'}.
• Interest paid: debit {'671 Interest'} (an expense), credit {'521 Bank'}.

sections.heading: Following the bank balance
sections.text:
Each financing transaction changes the bank balance: capital and loans add to it; repayments and interest take from it.
Capital {2000000} + loan {1500000} − repayment {300000} leaves {3200000} FCFA in the bank, and the loan account shows {1200000} FCFA still owed.

key_words.meaning: money or assets contributed by the owner
money borrowed that must be repaid
the cost of borrowing, an expense
a transaction that brings long-term funds

mistake.wrong: A loan is credited to Capital
mistake.right: A loan is credited to {'162'} Loans
mistake.why: The loan belongs to the bank and must be repaid; capital belongs to the owner.

worked_example.problem: Ms Ngozi starts a business: she pays {c} FCFA into the business bank account and the bank lends the business {l} FCFA. Give the entries and the bank balance.

cards.idea: The owner's contribution is credited to Capital.
A bank loan is credited to Loans.
Repaying the loan reduces both Loans and Bank.

check.prompt: A business receives capital of {c} FCFA and a loan of {l} FCFA into its bank account, then repays {r} FCFA of the loan. What is the bank balance (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: The repayment reduces the bank balance.
The loan received also adds to the bank.

pick.q: The owner pays 1 000 000 FCFA into the business bank account.
e: Reversed: money comes into the bank, so Bank is debited.
It is the owner's money, not a loan.

pick.q: The owner brings 300 000 FCFA in cash to start the business.
pick.y: Cash comes in from the owner.

pick.q: The owner contributes a car worth 2 500 000 FCFA to the business.
e: No money moves through the bank.
It is the owner's contribution, not a loan.
pick.y: The asset received is debited; capital is credited.

pick.q: The business receives a bank loan of 5 000 000 FCFA into its account.
e: A loan is not the owner's capital.
Interest is an expense paid later.

pick.q: The business repays 500 000 FCFA of its loan by bank transfer.
pick.y: The debt falls (debit Loans); Bank falls (credit).

pick.q: The business pays 60 000 FCFA interest on its loan by bank.
e: Interest does not reduce the loan itself.
It is paid from the bank.

questions.prompt: A business receives capital of {c} FCFA and a loan of {l} FCFA into its bank account, then repays {r} FCFA of the loan. What is the bank balance (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: The repayment reduces the bank balance.
The loan received also adds to the bank.

questions.prompt: A loan of {l} FCFA is repaid in equal yearly instalments of {i} FCFA. How much is still owed after {n} instalments (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: That is the amount repaid. The question asks what is still owed.

solution: Still owed = {l} − {i * n} = {answer} FCFA (the balance of {'162'} Loans).
